recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + Audit foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency foundation. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums in src/shared/types/ are consumed by every downstream module. Audit module provides the IAuditService interface and implementation that all state-changing operations depend on (GP-002).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Leave Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types and audit. Defines policy configuration (max days per leave type per fiscal year). Must exist before balance or request modules can validate against policy limits.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-policy (to know max days), audit, and shared-types. Manages balance lifecycle: initialization, deduction, credit. Enforces non-negative invariant. Must exist before leave-request can deduct on approval.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Leave Request module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-balance, leave-policy, audit, and shared-types. Orchestrates the full leave workflow: submit (validate against policy, check balance), approve (deduct balance, audit), reject (audit), cancel (credit balance, audit). This is the top-level orchestrating module.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (routes), application (services), domain (models/entities), infrastructure (repositories, db connection). Dependencies flow inward: routes → services → repositories → db. All service interfaces declared before implementations. No circular dependencies — verified DAG: shared-types ← audit ← leave-policy ← leave-balance ← leave-request. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums placed in src/shared/types/ because they are pure value types consumed by multiple modules. Every state-changing operation writes an audit record (GP-002). RBAC enforcement (GP-005) is applied at the route layer — manager-only endpoints (approveRequest, rejectRequest, getPendingRequests) vs employee endpoints. Input validation (GP-003) at route boundaries before service invocation.
